text: Thermal expansion of ocean water accounts for roughly 40% of observed sea-level rise since 1970.
Glacier melt in the Himalayas and Andes contributes a measurable fraction of sea-level rise.
Greenland ice sheet mass loss has accelerated since the 1990s, contributing ~0.7 mm/yr.
Antarctic ice sheet dynamics remain the largest uncertainty in long-term projections.
Satellite altimetry since 1993 shows a global mean sea-level rise of 3.4 mm/yr.
Ocean heat content is a dominant driver of steric sea-level change.
Tide gauge records extend the observational baseline back to the 19th century.
Groundwater depletion adds roughly 0.4 mm/yr to sea-level rise.
Coastal real estate markets are repricing risk in Florida and California.
Flood insurance premiums in the US have risen sharply since 2020.
Municipal bond yields in coastal cities reflect climate risk perceptions.
Property tax base erosion is a growing concern for coastal municipalities.
The mating habits of Antarctic krill are poorly understood.
The history of lighthouse construction is a niche academic field.
